newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil April 15-May 15 Fipe inflation at 0.30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil April 15-May 15 Fipe inflation at 0.30 pct.

text.p: Brazil's inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) was 0.30 percent between April 15 and May 15, down from 0.50 percent in the previous four week period, a Fipe official said.

Juarez Rizzieri, president of the Fipe institute, said a 1.61 percent drop in food prices helped to slow inflation in the period. He said he expects inflation for the whole of May at around 0.3 percent.
The Fipe president released the following breakdown of Fipe's weighted inflation index for April 15 through May 15:
- Food: -1.61 pct drop in the period
- Housing: 0.93 pct rise in the period
- Transportation: 0.13 pct rise in the period
- Personal expenses: -0.41 pct drop in the period
- Clothing: 6.54 pct rise in the period
- Health care: 0.92 pct rise in the period
- Education: 0.07 pct rise in the period
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures weekly.
